Electricity Department, Administration of Daman & Diu, Vidyut Bhavan, Somnath-Kachigam Road, Kachigam, Daman - 396 210 ** Respondents** # **Parties Present:** Shri Anand K Ganesan, Advocate, NTPC Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, NTPC Ms. Ritu Apurva Advocate, NTPC Shri Jai Dhanani Advocate, NTPC Shri Sriharsha Peechara, Advocate, TSSPDCL & TSNPDCL Shri S.Vallinayagam, Advocate, TANGEDCO Ms. B.Rajeswari, TANGEDCO Ms. R.Ramalakshmi, TANGEDCO Ms. R.Alamelu, TANGEDCO # ** ORDER ** The Petitioner, NTPC Limited has filed the present petition under Sections 62 and 79(1)(a) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Chapter-V of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 along with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions for Tariff determination from Renewable Energy Sources) Regulations, 2017 for determination of project specific levelised tariff for 100 MW Floating Solar Photo Voltaic Plant (in short ‘the Plant’) at water reservoir of Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station (RSTPS), Ramagundam in the State of Telangana. # ** Hearing dated 25.11.2019 ** 2. During the hearing on 25.11.2019, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner intended to use the solar power generation to replace the power _Order in Petition No. 368/GT/2019_ _Page 3 of 5_ supply from generating stations having high energy charge rate (ECR) of other thermal generating stations of Petitioner, namely Kudgi STPS and Solapur STPS respectively. However, the Commission, based on the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the prayers (ii) to (iv) in the said petition, may be considered as not pressed, directed the Petitioner, vide Record of Proceedings (ROP) to amend the petition, prior to seeking approval of levellised tariff of the Plant. Accordingly, the Petitioner has amended the petition vide affidavit dated 23.12.2019, after serving copies on the Respondents. 3. While so, the learned counsel for the Petitioner vide letter dated 16.12.2021 has informed that the Plant, which was expected to be commissioned during February 2021, could not be commissioned due to certain reasons beyond the control of the Petitioner including Covid-19 pandemic. It was also submitted that the declaration of commercial operation (COD) qua the entire capacity has been delayed and final cost is yet to be determined. Accordingly, the learned counsel for the Petitioner requested that the matter may be adjourned giving liberty to the Petitioner to move the matter upon achievement of COD of entire capacity. # ** Hearing dated 21.12.2021 ** 4. During the hearing of the petition through video conferencing on 21.12.2021, the learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in her letter dated 16.12.2021, as stated in paragraph 3 above. On a query of the Commission, as to the expected date of commercial operation of the Plant, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Plant is expected achieve COD during March-April 2022. On a further query by the Commission as to whether the Petitioner was willing to _Order in Petition No. 368/GT/2019_ _Page 4 of 5_ withdraw the petition, with liberty to file a fresh petition, taking into consideration the actual COD of the Plant and firmed up completed cost of the Plant, the learned counsel for the Petitioner agreed to the same, subject to adjustment of the filing fees deposited for this petition. 5. Accordingly, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present petition. The petition is, therefore, disposed of as withdrawn, with liberty to the Petitioner to file fresh petition, based on the actual COD of the Plant. The filing fees deposited by the Petitioner in respect of this petition, shall be adjusted against the fresh petition to be filed by the Petitioner, in terms of the liberty granted. 6. Petition No. 368/GT/2019 is disposed of in terms of the above. **_Sd/- Sd/- Sd/- Sd/-_ (Pravas Kumar Singh) (I.S. Jha) (Arun Goyal) Member Member Member** **(Arun Goyal) (P.K.
